pages.body:
Why This Book Exists


Have you ever read a comic book? Have you ever watched a superhero movie? There is always a hero. There is always a villain. There is always a rescue. The hero swoops in. The hero saves the day. The hero defeats the villain. We love heroes. We love their stories. We love their courage.


The Old Testament is full of heroes. It is full of figures. It is full of legends. Abraham. Joseph. Moses. David. Jonah. Esther. Ruth. These are the heroes of the Old Testament. These are the figures of the faith. But here is the secret. They are not the ultimate hero. They are not the final legend. They are shadows. They are echoes. They are patterns. They are clues. And every single one of them points to the ultimate hero. That hero is Jesus.


This book is for the curious. It is for the spiritual seeker who wants to understand the ultimate hero. It is for the person who wants to see the rescue. Over the next 30 days, we are going to look at 30 Old Testament figures. We are going to see their lives. We are going to see their stories. And we are going to see how they point to Jesus. They are the heroes. But Jesus is the ultimate hero.


The Value You Will Get


By the end of this book, you will not see the Old Testament as just a collection of old stories. You will see it as a gallery of heroes. You will see it as a pattern. You will see it as a blueprint. You will understand the Old Testament figures. You will understand their stories. You will understand why they matter today. You will have a new confidence in your faith. You will have a new love for your Bible. And you will have a new appreciation for the ultimate hero.


How to Use This Guide


This is a 30 day journey. Each day takes about 10 minutes. Read the hook. Read the ancient text...

The Hook
Have you ever stepped out in faith? Have you ever left something behind? Have you ever trusted God for something you could not see? Abraham did. He was a hero of faith. He left his home. He left his family. He went to a land he did not know. And his story is a clue about the ultimate hero.


The Ancient Text (OT)
"By faith Abraham, when called to go to a place he would later receive as his inheritance, obeyed and went, even though he did not know where he was going." - Hebrews 11:8 (Written around 60 A.D.)


Abraham had faith. He trusted God. He obeyed. He went. He did not know where he was going. He did not know what would happen. But he trusted God. He had faith. He was a hero.


The Fulfillment (NT)
"For you know the grace of our Lord Jesus Christ, that though he was rich, yet for your sake he became poor, so that you through his poverty might become rich." - 2 Corinthians 8:9


Jesus is the greater Abraham. Abraham left his home. Jesus left heaven. Abraham went to a land he did not know. Jesus came to a world he created. Abraham trusted God. Jesus trusted the Father. Abraham was a hero of faith. Jesus is the ultimate hero of faith.


The Verdict
Abraham was a hero. He stepped out in faith. Jesus is the greater hero. He stepped out of heaven. The pattern is exact. The shadow is precise. The hero is Jesus.


The Resonance
Do you need to step out in faith? Do you need to trust God for something you cannot see? Remember Abraham. Remember Jesus. Jesus took the greatest step of faith. He left heaven for you. He trusts the Father. You can trust Him.


The Prayer
God, thank you for the example of Abraham. Thank you for his faith. Thank you for Jesus. Thank you that He left heaven for me. Help me to step out in faith. Help me to trust you. Help me to follow the ultimate hero. Amen.

The Hook

"Then God said, 'Take your son, your only son, whom you love—Isaac—and go to the region of Moriah. Sacrifice him there as a burnt offering on a mountain I will show you.'" - Genesis 22:2 (Written around 2000 B.C.)


God tested Abraham. He asked him to sacrifice his son. His only son. The son he loved. Abraham was willing. He was willing to give up everything. He was willing to sacrifice. He was a hero.


The Fulfillment (NT)
"For God so loved the world that he gave his one and only Son, that whoever believes in him shall not perish but have eternal life." - John 3:16


Jesus is the greater Abraham. Abraham was willing to sacrifice his son. God actually sacrificed His Son. Abraham was willing to give up his only son. God gave up His only Son. Abraham was a hero of sacrifice. Jesus is the ultimate hero of sacrifice.


The Verdict
Abraham was a hero. He was willing to sacrifice. Jesus is the greater hero. He was the sacrifice. The pattern is exact. The shadow is precise. The hero is Jesus.


The Resonance
Do you need a sacrifice? Do you need someone to give everything for you? Remember Abraham. Remember Jesus. Jesus gave everything for you. He gave His life. He gave His love. You are the reason for His sacrifice.


The Prayer
God, thank you for the example of Abraham. Thank you for his willingness to sacrifice. Thank you for Jesus. Thank you that you gave your only Son for me. Help me to sacrifice for others. Help me to give generously. Help me to follow the ultimate hero. Amen.

The Hook
Have you ever needed a rescue? Have you ever needed a hero? Have you ever needed someone to save you? Abraham was a hero. He was a hero of faith. But he was not the ultimate hero. He was a shadow. He was an echo. He was a pattern. The ultimate hero is Jesus. He is the one who rescues. He is the one who saves. He is the one who delivers.


The Ancient Text (OT)
"Abram believed the LORD, and he credited it to him as righteousness." - Genesis 15:6 (Written around 2000 B.C.)


Abraham believed God. He trusted God. He had faith. And God credited it to him as righteousness. Abraham was a hero. But he pointed to a greater hero. He pointed to Jesus.


The Fulfillment (NT)
"For the Son of Man came to seek and to save the lost." - Luke 19:10


Jesus is the ultimate hero. He is the one who came to seek. He is the one who came to save. He is the one who came to rescue. He is the fulfillment of Abraham. He is the ultimate hero.


The Verdict

The Resonance

The Prayer
God, thank you for Abraham. Thank you for the heroes of the faith. Thank you for Jesus. Thank you for the ultimate hero. Help me to trust the hero. Help me to follow the hero. Help me to live in the rescue of the hero. Amen.



END MATTER


The 30-Day Hero Challenge
You have journeyed through 30 days of the ultimate hero. Now what? I challenge you to read the Gospel of John. It is 21 chapters. It will show you how Jesus is the fulfillment of every hero. As you read, look for the pattern. Look for the clues. Look for Jesus.


A Note on Faith
The heroes are evidence. They are evidence of a divine plan. But evidence does not save you. The heroes point to a person. The heroes point to Jesus. You can understand the heroes and still miss the ultimate hero. The invitation is for your heart. Jesus said, "Here I am! I stand at the door and knock. If anyone hears my voice and opens the door, I will come in." The heroes are on the table. The door is open. It is your choice.


About the Author
Christine A. writes for the spiritually curious. He is passionate about showing people the hidden wisdom of the Bible. He lives with his family and enjoys good coffee and long conversations with skeptics. He believes that honest questions deserve honest answers.


Coming Next: Parallel Lives
If you enjoyed this journey, the next book in the series goes deeper. Parallel Lives takes a 30 day look at discovering the ancient types of Jesus in the Old Testament. It is for the seeker who wants to go further.


Final Call to Action
Scan the QR code below to get the next book in the series. Visit our website to download a free reading plan. Join our community of seekers. The investigation is not over. The adventure is just beginning.



Cover Design Concept (The Seeker Edition)


A dark, midnight blue background. A glowing, ancient scroll unrolls across the cover. On the scroll, a gallery of ancient figures is drawn in silver lines. Abraham. Joseph. Moses. David. They are all pointing to a cross in the center. The title THE ULTIMATE HERO is in a bold, modern, metallic white font. The subtitle is in a clean, elegant serif font. The overall feel is mysterious, authoritative, and intellectually premium.
